The Admiral returns to Spain from his second voyage. Account of the Admirals Third Voyage, during which he discovered the continent of Paria; with the occurrences to his arrival in Hispaniola. arxiv-1608-06427.title: Arbitrarily regularizable graphs
arxiv-1608-06427.creator: Enrico Bozzo, Massimo Franceschet
arxiv-1608-06427.description: Abstract A graph is regularizable if it is possible to assign weights to its edges so that all nodes have the same degree. Weights can be positive, nonnegative or arbitrary as soon as the regularization degree is not null. Positive and nonnegative regularizable graphs have been thoroughly investigated in the literature.

arxiv-2301-01632.title: Subcritical sharpness for multiscale Boolean percolation
arxiv-2301-01632.creator: Barbara Dembin
arxiv-2301-01632.description: Abstract We consider a multiscale Boolean percolation on ℝ d \mathbb{R}^{d} with radius distribution μ \mu on [ 1 , + ∞ ) [1,+\infty) , d ≥ 2 d\geq 2 . The model is defined by superposing the original Boolean percolation model with radius distribution μ \mu with a countable number of scaled independent copies.

arxiv-2308-06694.title: IMPARTIAL AND PARTIZAN RESTRICTED CHOCOLATE BAR GAMES
arxiv-2308-06694.creator: Ryohei Miyadera
arxiv-2308-06694.description: Abstract Received: , Revised: , Accepted: , Published: Abstract In this paper, we consider impartial and partizan restricted chocolate bar games. In impartial restricted chocolate bar games, players cut a chocolate bar into two pieces along any horizontal or vertical line and eat whichever piece is smaller.

arxiv-2310-05836.title: Spontaneous locomotion of a symmetric squirmer
arxiv-2310-05836.creator: Richard Cobos, Aditya S. Khair, Ory Schnitzer
arxiv-2310-05836.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Richard Cobos, Aditya S. Khair, Ory Schnitzer. The squirmer is a popular model to analyse the fluid mechanics of a self-propelled object, such as a micro-organism. We demonstrate that some fore-aft symmetric squirmers can spontaneously self-propel above a critical Reynolds number.

arxiv-2405-03615.title: Nonnegative Matrix Factorization in Dimensionality Reduction: A Survey
arxiv-2405-03615.creator: Farid Saberi-Movahed, Kamal Berahmand, Razieh Sheikhpour, Yuefeng Li, Shirui Pan
arxiv-2405-03615.description: Abstract . Dimensionality Reduction plays a pivotal role in improving feature learning accuracy and reducing training time by eliminating redundant features, noise, and irrelevant data. Nonnegative Matrix Factorization (NMF) has emerged as a popular and powerful method for dimensionality reduction. Despite its extensive use, there remains a need for a comprehensive analysis of NMF in the context of dimensionality reduction.

arxiv-2410-03389.title: Quantum Effects in Ion Transport: A Thermodynamic Resource Theory Approach
arxiv-2410-03389.creator: Amin Mohammadi, Afshin Shafiee
arxiv-2410-03389.description: Abstract In recent years, understanding thermodynamics in the quantum regime has garnered significant attention, driven by advances in nanoscale physics and experimental techniques. In parallel, growing evidence supports the importance of quantum effects in various biological processes, making them increasingly relevant to quantum thermodynamics.

arxiv-2508-08430.title: Profiling Concurrent Vision Inference Workloads on NVIDIA Jetson - Extended
arxiv-2508-08430.creator: Abhinaba Chakraborty 1 Wouter Tavernier 1 Akis Kourtis 2 Mario Pickavet 1 Andreas Oikonomakis 2 Didier Colle 1
arxiv-2508-08430.description: Abstract The proliferation of IoT devices and advancements in network technologies have intensified the demand for real-time data processing at the network edge. To address these demands, low-power AI accelerators, particularly GPUs, are increasingly deployed for inference tasks, enabling efficient computation while mitigating the latency and bandwidth limitations of cloud-based systems.

M.H. and E.L. are grateful for funding from the European Research Council (ERC) under the European Unio
arxiv-2510-25326.creator: Irfan Glogić, Martina Hofmanová, Eliseo Luongo
arxiv-2510-25326.description: Abstract . We consider stochastically perturbed wave maps from ℝ 1 + d {\mathbb{R}}^{1+d} into 𝕊 d \mathbb{S}^{d} , in all energy-supercritical dimensions d ≥ 3 d\geq 3 . We show that corotational non-degenerate Gaussian additive noise leads to self-similar blowup with positive probability for any corotational initial data.

arxiv-2601-17937.title: “Label from Somewhere”: Reflexive Annotating for Situated AI Alignment DOI: XXXXXXX.XXXXXXX ISBN: 978-1-4503-XXXX-X/18/06 CCS: Human-centered computing Empirical studies in collaborative and social computing
arxiv-2601-17937.creator: Anne Arzberger, Céline Offerman, Ujwal Gadiraju, Alessandro Bozzon, Jie Yang
arxiv-2601-17937.description: Abstract . AI alignment relies on annotator judgments, yet annotation pipelines often treat annotators as interchangeable, obscuring how their social position shapes annotation. We introduce reflexive annotating as a probe that invites crowd workers to reflect on how their positionality informs subjective annotation judgments in a language model alignment context.

pmc-10648767.title: Effectiveness of Cerium Oxide Nanoparticles in Non-Alcoholic Fatty Liver Disease Evolution Using In Vivo and In Vitro Studies: A Systematic Review
pmc-10648767.creator: Cristian Sandoval, Carolina Reyes, Pamela Rosas, Karina Godoy, Vanessa Souza-Mello, Jorge Farías, Manuela Malatesta, Flavia Carton
pmc-10648767.description: Nonalcoholic fatty liver disease (NAFLD) describes a spectrum of liver abnormalities, from benign steatosis to nonalcoholic steatohepatitis (NASH). Because of their antioxidant capabilities, CeNPs have sparked a lot of interest in biological applications. This review evaluated the effectiveness of CeNPs in NAFLD evolution through in vivo and in vitro studies.

pmc-10675060.title: Remote Loading: The Missing Piece for Achieving High Drug Payload and Rapid Release in Polymeric Microbubbles
pmc-10675060.creator: Ghazal Rastegar, Mohammad Musa Salman, Shashank R Sirsi, Seung-Schik Yoo
pmc-10675060.description: The use of drug-loaded microbubbles for targeted drug delivery, particularly in cancer treatment, has been extensively studied in recent years. However, the loading capacity of microbubbles has been limited due to their surface area. Typically, drug molecules are loaded on or within the shell, or drug-loaded nanoparticles are coated on the surfaces of microbubbles.

pmc-11690136.title: SOCIAL PARTICIPATION OF PEOPLE LIVING WITH DEMENTIA IN GERMAN SHARED-HOUSING ARRANGEMENTS
pmc-11690136.creator: Karin Wolf-Ostermann, Julia Misonow, Janissa Altona
pmc-11690136.description: Aspects of social health are increasingly gaining more interest regarding research for people living with dementia (PlwD). Having a range of meaningful social relationships has been identified as crucial for healthy aging, defined by lower mortality rate, and better physical and mental health outcomes.

pmc-12431204.title: Macro-Microscopic Characterization and Long-Term Performance Prediction of Polyvinyl Chloride Under Hydrothermal Aging Based on Creep Behavior Analysis
pmc-12431204.creator: Hui Li, Xiaoxiao Su, Guan Gong, Aoxin Shao, Yanan Zheng
pmc-12431204.description: The creep behavior of rigid polyvinyl chloride (PVC) in hydrothermal environments can compromise its long-term stability and load-bearing capacity, potentially leading to deformation or structural failure. Understanding this degradation is critical for ensuring the durability and safety of PVC in engineering applications such as pipelines and building materials.

pmc-12621096.title: Dual roles of suberin deposition at the endodermal Casparian strip in manganese uptake of rice
pmc-12621096.creator: Toshiki Fujii, Naoki Yamaji, Jian Feng Ma, Ana Assunção
pmc-12621096.description: Rice roots are characterized by having two Casparian strips (CSs) at the exodermis and endodermis, where transporters for mineral nutrients are expressed. However, the exact role of the CS in expression of the transporters and subsequent nutrient uptake is poorly understood.

pmc-12734233.title: Old European Silkworm Breeds Reared in Early-20th-Century Bulgaria and Their Potential Use in Modern Sericulture
pmc-12734233.creator: Panomir Tzenov, Dimitar Grekov, Velislav Iliev, Vladimir A Lukhtanov, Haobo Jiang
pmc-12734233.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Simple SummaryThis paper focuses on the history of Bulgarian sericulture and the characteristics of silkworm breeds used towards the end of the 19th and the first half of the 20th century in Bulgaria.

pmc-13162101.title: The Impact of Medial Cortical Reduction on the Outcomes of Fixation in Unstable Intertrochanteric Fractures
pmc-13162101.creator: Parimal Vairagade, Devashish Barick, Sushil Mankar, Aniruddha Vaidya, Vaibhav Panchbhai
pmc-13162101.description: Introduction:Intertrochanteric fractures, especially unstable fractures, are common among the elderly and present significant challenges in terms of fracture healing and post-operative recovery. The medial cortex of the femur plays a crucial role in maintaining fracture stability and promoting healing. This study explores the impact of medial cortical reduction on the outcomes of fixation in unstable intertrochanteric fractures.

pmc-13340529.title: Renal Complement C3 Deposition is Associated with Glomerular Prothrombotic Milieu in Patients with IgA Nephropathy
pmc-13340529.creator: Yun Guo, Siqi Zheng, Shangmei Li, Zhennan Ye, Mianna Luo, Huafeng Liu
pmc-13340529.description: IntroductionComplement activation plays a central role in the pathogenesis of IgA nephropathy (IgAN); however, not all patients exhibit renal C3 deposition. Accumulating evidence suggests that complement activation is closely linked to coagulation activation and prothrombotic cellular responses.MethodsThis retrospective study was conducted using clinical and laboratory data obtained from the institutional clinical database of the Affiliated Hospital of Guangdong Medical University.

pmc-13518294.title: Wearable Movement‐Tracking for Prodromal Parkinson's Disease Detection: A Cross‐Country Validation Study
pmc-13518294.creator: Fabian Kahl, Ann‐Kathrin Schalkamp, Katarina Mary Gunter, Anja Ophey, Sinah Röttgen, Jamil Razzaque, Konstantin Kufer, Cynthia Sandor, Gereon R Fink, Elke Kalbe, Walter Maetzler, Clint Hansen, Stephan M Jonas, Michele T Hu, Lara Marie Reimer, Michael Sommerauer
pmc-13518294.description: BackgroundModels trained on accelerometer data have been proposed for detecting prodromal Parkinson's disease (PD). However, uncertainties in diagnosis timing in the UK Biobank (UKBB) may affect generalizability to other cohorts.ObjectivesThe aim of the study was to evaluate the performance of previously published models for prodromal PD detection in other international cohorts.
